topic: Food without a stove or microwave during a power cut

content.hook: You don't need a stove. You need a pantry.

slides.title: No stove? You need a *pantry*.
slides.body: Eating well during a power cut, no cooking needed.

slides.title: Pick foods that need *zero cooking*
slides.body: Canned beans, tuna, crackers, nut butter, dried fruit, ready-to-eat meals. Add a manual can opener.

slides.title: Eat *fridge first*, then pantry
slides.body: Keep doors shut. Fridge food first, then freezer, then shelf-stable food. Never cook indoors with a grill.

content.caption:
Food without a stove or microwave during a power cut: it's easier than it sounds.

You don't need a stove. You need a pantry that works without one.

1. Stock food you can eat as it is: canned beans, fish, crackers, nut butter, dried fruit, ready meals.
2. Keep a manual can opener with them.
3. Eat fridge food first, then freezer, then shelf-stable food. Keep the doors closed as much as you can.
4. Never use a grill or camp stove indoors.

Check the dates once or twice a year and swap in things your family actually likes.
